# Networks class

A CIDR membership set covering both address families — the entry point for most callers.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export declare class Networks 
```

## Remarks

Give it a mixed list of CIDR records and it sorts them into one [NetworkList](/api/net/latest/net.networklist/) per family, then dispatches each lookup to the list matching the address it is asked about. That indirection exists because the two families cannot share a buffer: an IPv6 record is 32 bytes against IPv4's 8.

Lookups are O(log n) within a family. Instances are immutable, so extending a set means constructing a new one.

A family with no networks is left unset rather than empty, and [Networks.includes()](/api/net/latest/net.networks.includes/) answers `false` for it — so a v4-only set safely answers questions about IPv6 addresses.

## Example


```typescript
const allowed = new Networks(['10.0.0.0/8', '2001:db8::/32']);

allowed.includes('10.1.2.3');     // true
allowed.includes('2001:db8::1');  // true
allowed.includes('8.8.8.8');      // false
```
